# Shipkeep

> Shipkeep is an open source (Apache-2.0), self-hosted platform as a service (PaaS) that deploys applications, databases and services to servers you own, without Kubernetes. It is in development and cannot be installed yet.

How it differs from panels that connect to servers over SSH:

- The control plane holds no SSH key. Each server runs an agent that opens an outbound mTLS connection to the control plane, enrolled with a one-time join token.
- The agent only runs a closed list of typed actions defined in a protobuf file. There is no generic shell or exec on the host, and no shell command is built from strings.
- Each application is described by a versioned `shipkeep.yml` in its repository. The web UI writes to that file instead of hiding state.
- The first release targets multiple servers with placement, health-based failover, a private WireGuard network and replicated routing.
- Upgrades are designed to take a snapshot first, and destructive actions need explicit confirmation.

Stack: Go (agent and CLI), TypeScript with NestJS (API) and Angular (web UI), PostgreSQL, Docker Engine API, Caddy.

## Project

- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/shipkeepdev/shipkeep): README, issues and roadmap
- [Website (English)](https://shipkeep.vercel.app/en): features, comparison with Coolify, Dokploy and Kamal, FAQ
